name: My SaaS Analytics
description: Demo connector over a small SaaS customer base: accounts, revenue, and product-usage events. Ships with Elliot so a fresh install has working tools, data, and an eval suite from the first minute.
instructions: Start with get_customer_overview when a question names a specific customer — it joins account and usage data into one compact result. Use list_customers to find accounts by plan or status, mrr_by_plan for revenue questions, and feature_adoption for usage questions. All results are bounded and sized for a context window; pass a smaller limit when you only need a few rows.

tools.name: Get Customer Overview
tools.description: Return one customer's full picture in a single call: account details, plan, monthly revenue, status, plus their total product-usage events and the time of their most recent activity.
tools.sql: SELECT c.id, c.name, c.email, c.plan, c.mrr, c.status, c.last_active_at, COUNT(e.id) AS total_events, MAX(e.ts) AS last_event_at FROM customers c LEFT JOIN events e ON e.customer_id = c.id WHERE c.id = :customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name, c.email, c.plan, c.mrr, c.status, c.last_active_at

parameters.name: customer_id
parameters.description: Numeric id of the customer to look up (exact match). Find ids with list_customers.

tools.name: List Customers
tools.description: List customers with their plan, monthly revenue, status, and last activity date, optionally narrowed to one plan or one lifecycle status. Most recently active first.
tools.sql: SELECT id, name, email, plan, mrr, status, last_active_at FROM customers WHERE (:plan IS NULL OR plan = :plan) AND (:status IS NULL OR status = :status) ORDER BY last_active_at DESC LIMIT :limit

parameters.name: plan
parameters.description: Keep only customers on this pricing plan (exact match).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Keep only customers in this lifecycle state (exact match).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of customers to return.

tools.name: MRR by Plan
tools.description: Aggregate monthly recurring revenue and customer count per pricing plan, highest revenue first, optionally restricted to one lifecycle status.
tools.sql: SELECT plan, SUM(mrr) AS total_mrr, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customers WHERE (:status IS NULL OR status = :status) GROUP BY plan ORDER BY total_mrr DESC

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Restrict the revenue rollup to customers in this lifecycle state (exact match).

tools.name: Churned Customers
tools.description: Return customers who have churned, with the plan and revenue that was lost and when they were last active. Most recently active first.
tools.sql: SELECT id, name, plan, mrr, last_active_at FROM customers WHERE status = 'churned' ORDER BY last_active_at DESC LIMIT 20

tools.name: Feature Adoption
tools.description: Count product-usage events per feature, most used first, optionally narrowed to a single event kind such as logins only.
tools.sql: SELECT feature, COUNT(*) AS usage_count FROM events WHERE (:event_type IS NULL OR event = :event_type) GROUP BY feature ORDER BY usage_count DESC

parameters.name: event_type
parameters.description: Count only events of this kind (exact match).

tools.name: New Signups
tools.description: Return the ten most recent customer signups with their contact details and chosen plan, newest first.
tools.sql: SELECT id, name, email, plan, signups_at FROM customers ORDER BY signups_at DESC LIMIT 10

skills.name: Weekly Account Review
skills.description: Compose a weekly health summary of the customer base: revenue by plan, recent churn, and which features are actually being used.
skills.instructions:
Run the review in three passes and keep each result compact.

1. Call mrr_by_plan with status "active" for the current revenue picture, then once more with no status to spot revenue sitting in churned accounts.
2. Call churned_customers and, for each account worth saving, call get_customer_overview with its customer_id to see whether usage dropped before the churn.
3. Call feature_adoption with event_type "feature_used" to rank features by real usage; call it again with no filter when login volume matters.

Finish with a short summary: total active MRR, plans trending up or down, at-risk accounts, and the top three features by usage.
skills.when_to_use: Use when asked for an account health check, churn review, or a weekly business summary of customers and usage.
